title: The Firmament
protagonist: a single wall-walker (POV recommendation in canon: close-third, one runner across the breach)
logline: For twelve generations they knew the truth: the world is a flat disc under a firmament, ringed by ice. They were right — about a world the size of a lifeboat. When the last seal fails, one of them walks through the ice wall and out onto the round Earth, where the old, forbidden verses come true one by one.
blueprint: Original dystopian sleeper. A sealed post-flare seedbank arcology, built flat because flat is the most efficient shape to shield, pressurise and light a closed world; the flat-disc cosmology was never a lie but an accurate description of the enclosure, mistaken for a description of the universe. Autopilot outlived its operators; a redacted scripture kept the world closed; devout maintenance workers passed the un-redacted original as samizdat. The reveal is fulfilment, not disproof.
market: literary dystopian / speculative sleeper — original IP, for the shelf
lineage: original — no borrowed IP. Kinship of engine only: the Truman-Show enclosure, the generation-ark reveal, the samizdat-scripture tradition. All world, cast, scenes, and beats original.
